_metadata_caption: Table 2 presents the zero-order correlations for selected baseline and daily diary variables. At baseline, the three age groups differed significantly from each other in neuroticism, F(2, 125) = 6.36, \eta^2 = 0.09, p < 0.01, years of education, F(2, 74) = 9.59, \eta^2 = 0.10, p < 0.001, and employment status, \chi^2 (4) = 53.72, p < 0.001. The three age groups did not differ from each other in extraversion, subjective health, life satisfaction, depressive symptoms, and marital status, all ps > 0.05. Results of Levene's test showed that the assumption of equal variances for the baseline and daily diary variables was met. For the test of multiple comparisons, we proceeded with Tukey's HSD test and the Games-Howell test because of the different sample sizes in the age groups. Results of the Tukey's HSD test and Games-Howell test were essentially identical. Here we report results of the Games-Howell test with the Holm method to adjust for the family-wise error rate. Older adults (M = 12.16; SD = 8.66) scored significantly (p < 0.05) lower on neuroticism compared to young adults (M = 18.30; SD = 8.83). For years of education, older adults (M = 19.82 years; SD = 4.17 years) reported significantly fewer years of education than young adults (M = 22.91  years; SD = 2.79  years). For the daily diary variables, the three age groups differed significantly in the mean level of gratitude across days, F(2, 125) = 6.23, \eta^2 = 0.09, p < 0.01. The Games-Howell test showed that older adults (M = 3.57; SD = 0.35) reported a higher level of gratitude across days than young adults (M = 2.81;SD = 0.41). In contrast, the three age groups did not differ significantly in the mean level of loneliness across days.
